- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often underestimates downside; add downward bias or adjust for volatility clustering.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; apply a “cool-down” rule to dampen subsequent forecast increases.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often fails to capture mean reversion; introduce a “reversion-to-mean” heuristic based on 10-15 day moving average.
- Forecast horizon 30d consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “lag correction” to reduce initial forecast values by 5-10% if sentiment is uncertain.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3-5 days, model often fails to adjust; trigger a “sentiment pivot” rule to re-calibrate forecast direction within 2-3 days.
